title: Sicilian orange salad
intro: Sliced oranges with red onion, black olives and good oil: sweet, salty and fresh.

steps.t: Peel the oranges with a sharp knife, removing all the white pith.
Slice them 5 mm thick and lay them on a plate, saving the juice.
Thinly slice the onion and soak it in cold water for 10 minutes to mellow it, then drain.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Scatter the onion and olives over the oranges; season with salt, pepper, oregano, oil and the saved juice.
Let it sit for 10 minutes before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Add paper-thin sliced fennel or a few smoked herring fillets.
Lovely next to grilled fish or a winter boiled-meat dinner.

title: Panzanella
intro: Stale Tuscan bread, ripe tomatoes, onion and basil: summer with nothing wasted.

steps.t: Cut the bread into chunks and soak in cold water with 1 tbsp vinegar for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile, cut the tomatoes into chunks, slice the cucumber and onion thinly, and put them in a big bowl with salt.
Squeeze the bread firmly by hand and crumble it over the vegetables.
Add the torn basil, the oil and the remaining vinegar and toss.
Let it sit for 30 minutes at room temperature so the bread soaks up the juices.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Use unsalted bread at least 2 days old; fresh bread turns to mush when soaked.
Add oil-packed tuna or anchovies to make it a summer main.

title: Greek salad
intro: Horiatiki: tomatoes, cucumber, olives and a slab of feta with oregano.

steps.t: Cut the tomatoes into wedges, the cucumber into thick half-moons, and the pepper and onion into thin rings.
Put them in a wide bowl with salt and vinegar and toss gently.
Add the olives and lay the feta on top in one whole slab.
Sprinkle the feta with oregano, pour over plenty of oil and serve with bread to mop up the juices.

tips.t: Salt only the vegetables, never the feta; it's salty enough.
Island style: add capers and a handful of purslane.

title: Tabbouleh
intro: The Lebanese salad where parsley is the star and bulgur just a touch.

steps.t: Rinse the bulgur, cover with the juice of 1 lemon and the water, and let it soften for 20 minutes.
steps.label: Bulgur

steps.t: Meanwhile, wash and dry the parsley and mint very well, then chop finely by hand.
Dice the tomatoes small, keeping their juice, and thinly slice the scallions.
Mix the herbs, tomatoes and scallions with the bulgur; dress with the other lemon's juice, oil and salt.
Serve right away, with lettuce leaves for scooping.

tips.t: The herbs must be bone-dry and chopped by knife; wet or blitzed, they turn to mush.
Part of a Lebanese mezze with hummus and baba ganoush.

title: Oi muchim
intro: Spicy Korean cucumber salad: crunchy, tangy and ready in minutes.

steps.t: Slice the cucumbers into 5 mm rounds, toss with the salt and let them sit for 15 minutes.
steps.label: Cucumbers

steps.t: Pour off the liquid and gently pat the cucumbers dry with paper towels.
Mix the grated garlic, chopped scallion, gochugaru, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil.
Toss the cucumbers in the dressing, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve cold right away.

tips.t: A perfect banchan with grilled meat, bulgogi or a bowl of rice.
A few drops of fish sauce add depth (but it's no longer vegan).

title: Solterito, broad bean and cheese salad
intro: Arequipa's salad of broad beans, corn, tomato, fresh cheese and olives.

steps.t: Blanch the broad beans in salted water, then plunge into iced water and slip off their skins.
steps.label: Broad beans

steps.t: Boil the corn cobs (pre-cooked: 3 minutes), let them cool and cut off the kernels with a knife.
steps.label: Corn

steps.t: Thinly slice the red onion, rinse it in cold water and drain well.
Dice the tomatoes and cheese into 1 cm cubes; finely chop the seeded chili and the parsley.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the beans, corn, onion, tomatoes, cheese, chili, olives and parsley; toss gently and serve straight away.

tips.t: Out of season, use frozen broad beans: blanch them for 4 minutes.
With fleshy red rocoto from a Latin shop, the heat is just like Arequipa's.

title: Som tam, pounded spicy salad
intro: Crunchy julienne pounded in a mortar with lime, fish sauce and chili: fresh and fiery.

steps.t: Cut the carrots and seeded cucumbers into long, thin julienne with a julienne peeler or a knife.
Cut the green beans into 3 cm pieces and halve the tomatoes. Juice the limes.
In a large mortar pound the garlic and chilies to a rough paste.
Add the beans and bruise them lightly, then the tomatoes, pounding gently so they release their juice.
Add the sugar, fish sauce and lime juice and stir with a spoon until the sugar dissolves.
Add the julienne and half the peanuts: pound lightly and turn with the spoon for 1 minute so it soaks up the dressing.
Taste: sour, salty, sweet and hot should be in balance. Serve at once with the remaining peanuts.

tips.t: Real som tam uses green papaya from Asian shops: peel it and julienne it like the carrots.
Vegan version: use soy sauce instead of fish sauce (no longer gluten-free).
As in Isan: with larb and sticky rice, eaten with your hands.

title: Fattoush, Lebanese bread salad
intro: Crisp vegetables, herbs and toasted pita with sumac and pomegranate molasses.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Tear the pitas into small pieces and toss with 2 tbsp oil and a pinch of sumac.

airfryer.t: Tear the pitas into small pieces and toss with 2 tbsp oil and a pinch of sumac.

steps.t: Bake at 200 °C for 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
steps.label: Pita

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 180 °C for 5 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden.

steps.t: Meanwhile chop the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, radishes and pepper; slice the scallions and chop the parsley and mint.
Whisk the lemon juice, crushed garlic, pomegranate molasses, sumac, salt and the rest of the oil.
At the last moment dress the vegetables, add the crisp bread, toss and sprinkle with more sumac.

tips.t: In summer add a handful of purslane: in Lebanon fattoush is never without it.
Add the bread only at the end, or keep half on top: it must stay crunchy.
A pinch of dried mint in the dressing makes it even more fragrant.

title: Kōhaku namasu, daikon carrot salad
intro: Sweet-sour daikon and carrot: red and white, the festive colours of Japanese New Year.

steps.t: Peel the daikon and carrot and cut them into thin 5 cm matchsticks, with a knife or a mandoline.
Toss them with the salt in a bowl and leave for 10 minutes, until they soften and release water.
steps.label: Salt

steps.t: Squeeze them hard by handfuls and discard all the liquid.
Stir the sugar into the rice vinegar until dissolved, then add the grated lemon zest.
Dress the vegetables, mix well and chill for at least 30 minutes so they absorb the flavour.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve cold in small mounds, draining off a little of the liquid.

tips.t: No daikon? Use thinly sliced radishes: sharper, but very good.
Yuzu zest from a Japanese shop instead of lemon gives the authentic aroma.
In a sealed jar it keeps 5 days in the fridge and improves with time.

title: Çoban salatası, shepherd's salad
intro: Diced tomato, cucumber and pepper with sumac onion: fresh, tangy and crunchy.

steps.t: Thinly slice the onion, rub it with half the sumac and a pinch of salt and leave for 10 minutes to soften.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Meanwhile dice the tomatoes, cucumbers (peeled in stripes) and peppers into small, even 1 cm cubes.
Finely chop the parsley and mint.
Combine everything in a bowl and dress at the last minute with lemon juice, oil and salt.
Toss gently and finish with the remaining sumac. Serve at once.

tips.t: Dice everything by knife into small, equal cubes: that's the secret of a true çoban.
A drizzle of pomegranate molasses (nar ekşisi) makes it sweet-sour, Gaziantep style.
Perfect with tavuk şiş or grilled köfte, with bread to mop up the juices.

title: Coleslaw
intro: Shredded cabbage and carrot in a creamy, tangy dressing: the barbecue side.

steps.t: Remove the outer leaves and core and shred both cabbages very finely with a knife or mandoline.
Toss the cabbage with the salt in a colander and leave it: it releases water so the dressing stays creamy.
steps.label: Cabbage

steps.t: Meanwhile grate the carrots and whisk the mayonnaise (shop-bought is fine), vinegar, sugar, mustard and pepper in a big bowl.
Squeeze the cabbage firmly with your hands and add it to the dressing with the carrots.
Mix well, cover and chill so the flavours come together. Stir again before serving.
steps.label: Chill

tips.t: Half a teaspoon of celery seed is the classic American touch.
Lighter, mayo-free version: 4 tbsp oil, 3 tbsp cider vinegar and 1 tbsp sugar.
Perfect with fried chicken, ribs or piled into a pulled pork sandwich.
